task.title: Reply to an angry customer about a late order
task.brief: You work in chat and email support for an online shop. Read the customer's email and the internal notes below. Write the email reply you would send. Take about 15 minutes. A good reply: greets the customer by name, says sorry without blaming anyone, explains in plain words what went wrong, gives both options with clear dates, says what you will do next and by when, and ends politely. Keep it short and easy to read. Do not promise anything the notes do not allow.
task.material:
CUSTOMER EMAIL
From: Farhan Qureshi
Subject: WHERE IS MY ORDER??

I ordered a mixer grinder (order NM48213, Rs 3,499, paid by UPI) on 4 Nov. You said delivery by 10 Nov. It is 16 Nov today. Tracking is stuck for 5 days. I chatted with your team on 12 Nov and they promised a call back. Nobody called. My mother's old mixer is broken and we need this. Either deliver it now or give my money back. Very disappointed.

INTERNAL NOTES (not for the customer to see)
- Parcel is held at the Hyderabad hub. The pincode in the address (500083) does not match the area (Kukatpally, 500072).
- If the customer confirms the right pincode today, re-delivery can happen within 2 days.
- Or a full refund to the UPI account can be made; it takes 5 to 7 working days.
- The 12 Nov call-back was missed. You may offer a Rs 200 coupon for the trouble.
key_points: Greets the customer by name and apologises sincerely, including for the missed call-back
Explains the pincode mismatch simply, without blaming the customer
Asks the customer to confirm the correct pincode
Offers re-delivery within 2 days of confirmation
Offers a full refund to UPI in 5 to 7 working days as the other option
Mentions the Rs 200 coupon for the trouble
Says what happens next and by when, with a polite close
Does not promise anything beyond the notes or share internal wording

rubric.label: Tone and empathy
rubric.guide: 0 = rude, cold or blaming; 3 = polite but stiff; 5 = warm, calm, owns the mistake

rubric.label: Correct facts and options
rubric.guide: 0 = wrong facts or false promises; 3 = mostly right, one option or date missing; 5 = both options, dates and coupon right

rubric.label: Clarity
rubric.guide: 0 = confusing or very long; 3 = clear but wordy; 5 = short, simple, easy to act on

rubric.label: Next steps
rubric.guide: 0 = no next step; 3 = next step vague; 5 = clear action for the customer and for us, with timing
